entries.subject: The color of the photosphere
entries.finding: A Planck spectrum at the published 2,700 K (Dupuy et al. 2023, the pair's combined spectrum), through the CIE 1931 2-degree observer into sRGB with the D65 white.

entries.subject: Limb darkening of the sphere
entries.finding: No fit of this star's limb exists, so the sphere is darkened by the quadratic TESS law Claret (2017) computes from PHOENIX model atmospheres at 2,700 K and log g 5.13, from the record's mass and radius: a model. It replaced the uniform disc of the first version.

entries.subject: Gaia DR3's BP/RP spectrum of the pair as the color
entries.finding: Gaia DR3 source 3526198184723289472 has a BP/RP spectrum (has_xp_continuous true, no sampled spectrum published), but it is the combined light of A and B, which Gaia does not resolve, and the pair is faint in BP (18.0 mag), where the visible color is weighted. The paper temperature is used for both stars instead.
entries.revisitWhen: Gaia resolves the pair, or a spectrum of A alone is published.

entries.subject: A measured radius of either star
entries.finding: No interferometric or eclipse radius of A or B is published. Climent et al. (2022) adopt 0.12 solar radii for each from the Chabrier et al. (2000) models at the pair's age and mass (0.12 to 0.14 over those ranges); that model value is used.
entries.revisitWhen: A radius of either component is measured.
